findings.message:
I think both this check and the one in `SysFsType::create` are wrong.

https://github.com/asterinas/asterinas/blob/3b606f5b6c127c1a5631d8c2c652d23b9a8f9937/kernel/src/syscall/mount.rs#L155-L184

The user space is allowed to mount a ProcFS, SysFS, or ConfigFS multiple times; for example, when each container will mount these special FSes. This means that the corresponding `FsType::create` may be invoked multiple times. So this function should simply return the FS singleton if it is already initialized.
findings.tp_fp_justification: ConfigFsType::create rejects second mount with Errno::EBUSY by checking CONFIG_SINGLETON.is_completed(). But Linux allows special pseudo-filesystems (procfs, sysfs, configfs) to be mounted multiple times — containers each mount them independently. The correct behavior is to return the ConfigFs singleton when already initialized, not reject. tatetian points out the same bug also exists in SysFsType::create.
